name: Bai Fen
description: Bai Fen (literally 'Hundred Points') is a foundational Chinese trick-taking game that serves as the progenitor to more complex multi-deck games like Tractor (Sheng Ji). Played with a single 54-card deck, it is a game of partnership survival where the Attacking team tries to capture specific point cards (5s, 10s, and Kings) while the Defending team protects their lead. It features a trump system where a trump rank is rotated and combined with jokers to create a powerful hierarchy.

overview.description: Bai Fen (literally 'Hundred Points') is a foundational Chinese trick-taking game that serves as the progenitor to more complex multi-deck games like Tractor (Sheng Ji). Played with a single 54-card deck, it is a game of partnership survival where the Attacking team tries to capture specific point cards (5s, 10s, and Kings) while the Defending team protects their lead. It features a trump system where a trump rank is rotated and combined with jokers to create a powerful hierarchy.

history.origins: Originating in Northern China as a simplified version of the older 'Zheng Fen' (Compete for Points) games. It standardized the '100 Point' economy of a single deck, making it accessible to a wider audience before the 1980s explosion of multi-deck 'Tractor' variants.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Single-deck point games emerge in family social circles.
1950s: Rules standardized across urban centers like Beijing and Shanghai.
1980s: The game evolves into 'Ba Shi Fen' (80 Points) and 'Tractor' using two decks.
Present: Still played in households that prefer the tighter, more mathematical constraints of a single deck.
history.cultural: Frequently played at weddings and festivals; it is seen as a game of cooperation and shared fortune.
history.evolution: The transition from 'Bai Fen' to 'Tractor' marked a shift from individual card tracking to pattern-based 'sequential' play.

setup.deck: One standard 52-card deck plus both Jokers (Red and Black).
setup.dealing: The deck is shuffled and players draw one card at a time until the deck is exhausted. The dealer role rotates clockwise.

rules.objective: The 'Attacking' team must collect at least 40 points in their tricks to 'win' the round. Collecting 100 points (all point cards) is a 'cleaning' victory.
rules.gameplay: Standard trick-taking rules apply. Players must follow suit if possible. The highest trump wins the trick; if no trumps, the highest card of the led suit wins.
keyRules: The 'Kicker': On the final trick, if the Attacker wins, the points in the final trick are multiplied (doubled or tripled depending on the house rules).
No Trump: In some variants, if no trump suit is declared, only Rank cards and Jokers are trumps.

strategy.basic: Bankers should always lead their strongest non-trump suits early to force the Attackers to spend their trumps on low-value tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Point Control: If you are the Attacker and know you can't win the trick, throw your point cards (5s, 10s) to your PARTNER if they are likely to win it.
strategy.advanced: The Void Tactic: Try to empty your hand of a low-value suit early so you can 'Trump In' (ruff) when that suit is led, stealing the points from the Bankers.
tips: Count the 5s and 10s. There are only four of each rank. Knowing how many are left in play is the difference between a master and a novice.
Never lead a King unless you are certain it is the highest card remaining; losing a King is a 10-point swing to the opponent.

variations.name: Da Bai Fen (Great 100)
variations.description: Uses a 'Leveling' system where winning a hand allows you to promote your Trump Rank (e.g., from 2 to 3).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant shares the same base rules as Bai Fen; only the level-based trump rank progression changes and is modeled in description.

scoring.description: Points are tallied at the end of each hand. Only the Attacking team's points are counted towards the 'Win/Loss' threshold.
scoring.winCondition: 40 points = Attacker wins. 80 points = Attacker wins big (+2 levels in Sheng Ji variants).

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the classic Chinese strategy game that inspired a generation. Bai Fen is a high-tension partnership game where every 5, 10, and King is a battlefield. Use your Jokers wisely as you navigate the shifting ranks of the Chinese Level system to steal the points and claim the Banker's seat.
